execute: Separate identity, ownership/scope, current reachability, deployment and CVE applicability. Record observation time, resolver/environment, query type and source version. CT/SAN and APK/OpenAPI names are candidates. For DNS retain transport status, rcode and answer sections; compare known-normal and candidate-negative names, considering wildcards. Empty output is not NXDOMAIN; 198.18.0.0/15 covers only 198.18.* and 198.19.*. Attribute HTTP/TLS via resolver, proxy, Host/SNI and endpoint identity; 000 or 200 alone does not establish liveness. Check authoritative advisories and actual component/version/configuration before inferring CVE applicability.
review: Support each attribution claim with its own raw evidence and conditions. Fingerprints, common names, shared payloads and watchlist entries do not establish ownership, shared backend or vulnerability. Wildcard/portal controls or incompatible versions may refute a specific inference. Unknown observer or source keeps it inconclusive. Stop dependent branches; reopen for valid resolution, ownership, service identity or verified advisory/deployment evidence.
